report.source_text: After the diagnosis of metastatic CC, she was referred to and followed closely by the oncology service and a combined chemotherapy regimen [EMA/CO (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D, cyclophosphamide, and vincristine)] was started for her. To reduce the risk of pulmonary hemorrhage, we considered low-dose induction chemotherapy with 100 mg/m2/day of intravenous etoposide and 20 mg/m2/day of intravenous cisplatin on days one and two every 7 days for two courses prior to starting the EMA/CO regimen. Serum HCG level monitoring demonstrated a good response to treatment. The β-HCG titer was reduced to 125 mUI/m after three cycles of chemotherapy and the patient is currently continuing her chemotherapy process.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old postpartum female (day 1 after normal vaginal delivery at 38+4 weeks) presented with acute-onset dyspnea, left hemithorax pain, and severe respiratory distress (SpO2 88%, RR 35, HR 146). Physical examination revealed reduced left lung sounds and a suburethral vaginal lesion. Initial workup demonstrated left hemothorax with bilateral pulmonary nodules (41mm right upper lobe, 34mm left lung) on HRCT suggestive of metastases. Serum β-HCG was markedly elevated at 1,254,800 mUI/m. Pelvic ultrasound revealed a 31×21mm heterogeneous uterine cavity mass with low-resistant peripheral vessels. Brain MRI showed no intracranial metastases. The diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma (Stage III, high-risk) was established based on clinical (vaginal lesion), radiological (pulmonary metastases, uterine mass), and biochemical (β-HCG >1,000,000) evidence. Treatment commenced with low-dose induction chemotherapy (etoposide/cisplatin) to prevent pulmonary hemorrhage, followed by EMA/CO regimen. The patient demonstrated a good response with β-HCG declining to 125 mUI/m after three cycles and was continuing chemotherapy at last follow-up.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Postpartum presentation (day 1) with acute respiratory distress and suburethral vaginal lesion
Bilateral pulmonary metastases (41mm right, 34mm left) with left hemothorax on HRCT
Markedly elevated serum β-HCG at 1,254,800 mUI/m consistent with choriocarcinoma
Uterine cavity mass (31×21mm) with vascularity on transvaginal ultrasound indicating primary gestational trophoblastic disease
Absence of cerebral metastases on brain MRI (Stage III rather than IV)
Diagnosis directed by elevated β-HCG plus clinical and radiological evidence of metastases
Treatment with EMA/CO chemotherapy following low-dose induction (etoposide/cisplatin)
Favorable treatment response with β-HCG decline from 1,254,800 to 125 mUI/m after three cycles

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Markedly elevated β-HCG and postpartum context with uterine mass make primary lung cancer unlikely
Bilateral pulmonary nodules rather than filling defects, plus elevated β-HCG and uterine mass point to metastatic disease rather than thromboembolism
Brain MRI showed normal intracranial appearances with no evidence of metastases (E006)

remaining_uncertainties: Histopathological confirmation from biopsy was not documented in the available evidence; diagnosis appears to have been made on clinical, radiological, and biochemical grounds per the final diagnosis statement
Long-term outcome beyond three cycles of chemotherapy is not documented
No documented evaluation for liver or other abdominal metastases beyond the pelvic ultrasound
